_README: Copy this to employers.json and REPLACE EVERY PLACEHOLDER. employers.json is gitignored.
*** THIS FILE NEVER LEAVES YOUR MACHINE. ***
It holds factual assertions about named companies, some of them second-hand. That is
fine as a private note and unusable anywhere else. It must never reach a CV, a cover
letter, an oversight export, or anything a third party reads. If anyone asks why you
are not interested in an employer, the answer is 'it is not the right fit for me' and
nothing further. Repeating a second-hand allegation about a named company is a risk to
watch  — complete coverage of an employer, not just what they syndicate to job boards
avoid  — filters the radar BEFORE scoring, so settled questions cost nothing
'declined' is a third thing and deliberately does not filter: a role you turned down on
a commute or a start date can legitimately come back. It marks those rows with a dagger.

_comment: One entry per employer you actually want watched. Give it whichever route reaches
them — the point is complete coverage of that employer, not one adapter.
workday     three separate values, all visible in their careers URL.
If their careers site is NOT Workday, check anyway: search the page
source for 'myworkdayjobs' or 'myworkdaysite'. Big employers often
put a different front end over a Workday back end, and the Apply
links give the tenant away.
oracle      two values, both in the careers URL:
https://<host>/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/<site>/jobs
greenhouse  board token, from boards.greenhouse.io/<token>
lever       company slug, from jobs.lever.co/<slug>
query       the fallback and the weakest route — a search term rather than their
own board, so it sees only what they choose to syndicate.
An entry with no route at all is reported loudly, because 'watching' them would
otherwise be false.
avoid_divisions excludes part of an employer you otherwise want. Division names
usually appear in the job title, which is where this looks.
watch.why: <why you want to work there — this is for you, not for a cover letter>
avoid_divisions: <a division inside them you would not work in>

_comment: reason AND basis, both. 'Their published policy says X' and 'someone who worked
there told me X' are both legitimate reasons to decline an employer and completely
different kinds of claim — the basis is what decides how durable the exclusion is.
basis: published | personal-experience | word-of-mouth | reported
since: exclusions go stale. Companies change ownership, policy and management, and
the radar asks about anything older than two years.
divisions: leave empty to exclude the whole employer.
A category catches employers you have never heard of, which a name list cannot.
Ask yourself whether the objection is to one company or to the whole sector — it is
often genuinely unclear, and the answer changes how much this filters.
Categories worth considering: gambling, tobacco, arms, payday lending, or a
documented employment-practices record.
match: whole words, checked against the description as well as the title, so this
runs after descriptions are fetched. Without a description a sector cannot be
judged from a company name at all.
match: <a word that appears in such a posting>

_comment: Assessed and turned down — NOT a principled exclusion, and deliberately not a
filter. Recording it separately means a re-appearance is decided in seconds
instead of researched again from scratch.
